exposure: cesarean hysterectomy performed by gynecologic oncologists
type of surgeon performing cesarean hysterectomy (gynecologic oncologist vs Ob/Gyn specialist)
cesarean hysterectomy performed by Ob/Gyn specialists
outcome: maternal morbidity composite (estimated blood loss >2 L, ICU admission, intraoperative acidosis, post-operative length of stay >4 days)
cohort: 122 singleton, non-anomalous pregnancies complicated by Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) at the University of Texas Health San Antonio Placenta Accreta program from 2010 to 2021
finding: While gynecologic oncologists performed PAS cesarean hysterectomies in more complex cases, their involvement was not associated with increased composite maternal morbidity after adjusting for confounders.
